cards.front: Angles on a straight line add up to...
cards.say: Angles on a straight line add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

cards.front: Angles around a point add up to...
cards.say: Angles around a point add up to three hundred and sixty degrees, a full turn.

cards.front: Angles in a triangle add up to...
cards.say: Angles in a triangle add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

cards.front: Angles in a quadrilateral add up to...
cards.say: Angles in a quadrilateral add up to three hundred and sixty degrees.

cards.front: How big is a right angle?
cards.back: 90 degrees. It is a quarter turn, like the corner of a book.
cards.say: How big is a right angle? Ninety degrees. It is a quarter turn, like the corner of a book.

figure.alt: An angle of 90 degrees drawn with two arms

cards.front: How big is a half turn?
cards.say: How big is a half turn? One hundred and eighty degrees, a straight angle.

cards.front: How big is a three quarter turn?
cards.say: How big is a three quarter turn? Two hundred and seventy degrees.

cards.front: What is an acute angle?
cards.say: What is an acute angle? An angle smaller than ninety degrees.

figure.label: Acute
figure.alt: An angle of 40 degrees drawn with two arms

cards.front: What is an obtuse angle?
cards.back: An angle bigger than 90 degrees but smaller than 180 degrees.
cards.say: What is an obtuse angle? An angle bigger than ninety degrees but smaller than one hundred and eighty degrees.

figure.label: Obtuse
figure.alt: An angle of 120 degrees drawn with two arms

cards.front: What is a reflex angle?
cards.back: An angle bigger than 180 degrees but smaller than 360 degrees.
cards.say: What is a reflex angle? An angle bigger than one hundred and eighty degrees but smaller than three hundred and sixty degrees.

figure.label: Reflex
figure.alt: An angle of 250 degrees drawn with two arms

cards.front: Angles on a straight line: 125 degrees and x. Find x.
cards.say: Angles on a straight line: one hundred and twenty five degrees and x. Find x. Fifty five degrees. One hundred and eighty minus one hundred and twenty five equals fifty five.

cards.front: Angles on a straight line: 90 degrees, 40 degrees and x. Find x.
cards.say: Angles on a straight line: ninety degrees, forty degrees and x. Find x. Fifty degrees, because ninety plus forty is one hundred and thirty, and one hundred and eighty minus that is fifty.

cards.front: Angles around a point: 100 degrees, 120 degrees and x. Find x.
cards.say: Angles around a point: one hundred degrees, one hundred and twenty degrees and x. Find x. One hundred and forty degrees, because three hundred and sixty minus two hundred and twenty is that.

cards.front: A triangle has angles 60 degrees and 70 degrees. Find the third angle.
cards.say: A triangle has angles sixty degrees and seventy degrees. Find the third angle. Fifty degrees, because sixty plus seventy is one hundred and thirty, and one hundred and eighty minus that is fifty.

cards.front: A triangle has a right angle and a 35 degree angle. Find the third angle.
cards.say: A triangle has a right angle and a thirty five degree angle. Find the third angle. Fifty five degrees, because one hundred and eighty minus one hundred and twenty five equals fifty five.

cards.front: How big is each angle in an equilateral triangle?
cards.back: 60 degrees. Three equal angles share 180 degrees: 180 ÷ 3 = 60.
cards.say: How big is each angle in an equilateral triangle? Sixty degrees. Three equal angles share one hundred and eighty degrees, and one hundred and eighty divided by three equals sixty.

cards.front: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of 40 degrees. How big are the two equal base angles?
cards.say: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of forty degrees. How big are the two equal base angles? Seventy degrees each, because one hundred and eighty minus forty, then halved, is seventy.

cards.front: A quadrilateral has angles 90, 90, 90 degrees and x. Find x.
cards.say: A quadrilateral has angles ninety, ninety and ninety degrees, and x. Find x. Ninety degrees, because three right angles make two hundred and seventy, and three hundred and sixty minus that is ninety.

cards.front: A quadrilateral has angles 110, 80, 70 degrees and x. Find x.
cards.say: A quadrilateral has angles one hundred and ten, eighty and seventy degrees, and x. Find x. One hundred degrees, because those add to two hundred and sixty, and three sixty minus that is one hundred.

cards.front: What are vertically opposite angles?
cards.back: Angles opposite each other where two straight lines cross. They are equal.
cards.say: What are vertically opposite angles? Angles opposite each other where two straight lines cross. They are equal.

cards.front: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
cards.say: How many right angles does a rectangle have? Four. All four corners are ninety degrees.

cards.front: What tool do we use to measure angles?
cards.say: What tool do we use to measure angles? A protractor.

cards.front: Do the angles of a bigger triangle add up to more than 180 degrees?
cards.back: No. Every triangle, big or small, has angles that add up to 180 degrees.
cards.say: Do the angles of a bigger triangle add up to more than one hundred and eighty degrees? No. Every triangle, big or small, has angles that add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
